title: declarative-econ-workflows-cli-and-quant-fallback-guard
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces declarative econ workflows CLI, default batch/cache profiles, quantization fallback presets, and unit-econ-lint checks. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via tenant defaults.
description: Motivation: Teams repeatedly tune batching/caching/quantization by hand. This PR introduces a lightweight declarative workflows layer (econflow) and a CLI to generate and deploy tenant-safe defaults, plus runtime-safe quantization fallback presets and a unit-econ validation step. Goals: 1) Make sensible batching/cache/quant defaults easy to apply across tenants; 2) Provide rollback-safe quant fallback profiles when aggressive quantization degrades quality; 3) Ship unit economics checks that run as part of CI and the console onboarding flow; 4) Emit telemetry to validate cost/latency/quality tradeoffs in canary rollouts. What this PR includes: - New CLI: `redwood-econctl` with commands: `init`, `plan`, `apply`, `rollback`, `dry-run` and `simulate` for deterministic cost projections. - Declarative schema: YAML-driven econflow manifests (examples in docs/ and examples/) that express batch shapes, cache TTLs, quant profile priorities, and rollback rules. - Runtime hook: serverside admission filter that enforces tenant opt-in and validates manifests against a safety policy. - Quantization fallback: three fallback tiers (conservative, moderate, aggressive) with automatic loss-monitoring thresholds and traffic-split logic. - Unit economics linter: `unit-econ-lint` (CI plugin) that flags manifest changes likely to increase per-token cost >5% or expected latency regressions >10ms. - Telemetry: added metrics: econflow.apply_count, econflow.simulated_savings, econflow.rollback_triggers and prefiller.batch_shape_histogram. - Small UI surface: Console entries for applying and previewing econ manifests (Console PR will follow). Rollout plan: - Feature flag behind `econflow.enable` (default off). - Start with internal tenants + beta customers; run `simulate` job against historical traces to estimate impact. - Canary apply to 5% traffic then 25% then full rollout with automatic rollback on degradation signals. Checklist: - [x] Schema + examples - [x] CLI implementation - [x] Runtime admission and validation - [x] Telemetry hooks - [x] Unit-econ-lint integration - [x] Tests: unit + integration + e2e sandboxed simulation Known limitations and follow-ups: - The Console integration is minimal; richer UI will be a follow-up PR. - Auto-suggested defaults are conservative; we plan heuristics tuning after telemetry. - Simulation assumes representative historical traces; some tenant workloads may need manual tuning. Related: ENG-4219 (econflow design doc), ENG-4320 (quant-fallback thresholds).
